title: The Fascia Lata as a Model for the Mechanical,  Sensory, and Clinical Roles of Deep Fascia
content: Background: Fascia has been overlooked throughout most of the history of anatomy, but many recent studies have begun to showcase its role. The ventral thigh has been extensively studied in various fields, including anatomy, biomechanics, physiotherapy, histology, and orthopedics. Therefore, the fascia lata is a good model for synthesizing the recent knowledge accumulated from studying this organ. Methods: A review was constructed to describe the characteristics of the deep fascia, with articles highlighting the main roles of the fascia lata selected for this purpose. Results: Forces travel through the fascia lata according to knee and hip positioning, optimizing energy sparing. When the knee is extended, the forces are transmitted to the iliotibial band whereas, when the knee is flexed, the forces are transmitted to the patella. Additionally, the fascia lata is a propri-oceptive organ. Its lengthening during a stretch is felt as pain while the mechanical tension is felt as a feeling of tension. The fascia lata can be lengthened and maybe reinforced by stretching training. Moreover, it is likely that its stiffness can be responsible for a few of the main running pathologies. Conclusions: The fascia lata may provide an insight into the major roles of the fascial tissue. This literature review put in relief a few gaps in fascia histology and bridging these lacunes would be profitable to better understand the physiology underlying its proprioceptive role. Finally, a better understanding of fascia physiology may improve clinical reasoning in various medical specialties.
